text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The current leu exchange rate is unattractive to Romanian exporters who say it is artificially buoyed up.
ADEVARUL
- The IMF is concerned over Romania's short-term private foreign debt. Romanian commercial banks launched promissory notes worth more $1 billion in international markets.
TINERETUL LIBER
- The Bucharest commodities exchange is organising an auction on Friday to sell off 25,000 tonnes of scrap iron.
ZIUA
- Only 15 percent of Romania's helicopter fleet is operational. The rest cannot be overhauled for lack of funds.
LIBERTATEA
- Foreign investment in Romania stands at $2.03 billion at end-September.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The Communications Ministry expects offers from international companies to evaluate bids made for a GSM system in Romania.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Polish Lublin vans will be assembled in Romania and sold as Daewoo Lublin under a contract between the Polish plant and Romanian car makers Rodae SA and ARO SA.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Wim Van Velzen, president of the Christian-Democrat European Union (UECD) said "the campaign of manipulation of (the ruling) Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) through telephone polls is incredible".
- The newspaper asks what the real number of eligible Romanians is as various institutions mention figures varying between 15.8 million and 17.7 million.
- The opposition Christian Democrat National Peasant Party (PNT-CD) urges the ruling PDSR to stop the alleged fake telephone opinion poll.
ADEVARUL
- Full-page report on four years of activity of Romania's parliament. As many as 505 laws adopted by the two houses were signed into law by President Ion Iliescu.
- Romania is within a group of countries which could join the European Union in a second or even third wave, said Wim Van Velzen.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The elite protection service (SPP) says in a statement it provides protection for 14 of the 16 presidential candidates during the campaign ahead of the November 3 general polls.
- Journalists who disclosed the case of the fake telephone poll are being investigated by the police.
- Parties have been given total subsidies worth 2.5 billion lei ($766 million) until October 1996.
ZIUA
- Wim van Velzen, UECD president, said the Romanian government was likely to try to rig the elections as the ruling PDSR uses fake phone polls and attacks the opposition in campaign video clips.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The newspaper publishes the appeal by Emil Constantinescu, presidential candidate of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR), to defend democracy and freedom for November 3 elections. It also prints the response of the ruling PDSR.
COTIDIANUL
- Editorial says the ruling PDSR is gearing up for mass fraud in the November 3 polls.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The newspaper publishes a report on "Transylvanian Gypsies wearing hats". ($=3,262 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
